name: Adventor (A-komunita)
summary: Prague community centre and self-help organisation for autistic children, teenagers and adults, running individualised support, an antiquarian bookshop, and inclusion projects with mixed autistic and non-autistic teams.
notes: Runs the KC Kopec community centre. Full member of EUCAP. Site blocks bare curl requests (403) but is reachable with a browser user agent and was read in full via fetch.

name: CEPAMA (Committee for the Promotion and Support of Autistic Girls and Women)
name_local: Comité para la Promoción y Apoyo de las Niñas y Mujeres Autistas
summary: Spanish association of autistic women working on the rights, visibility and research access of autistic girls and women, including a participatory research project with the University of Lisbon on employment, education and healthcare.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. Site states 'somos mujeres autistas' (we are autistic women) and describes governance by autistic women.

name: Voz do Autista (APVA)
summary: Aveiro-based self-advocacy association of autistic adults, parents and autistic health/education professionals, running an online rights-guidance service, employment support projects and free resources for autistic people.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. Describes itself as 'an association of autists, for autists.'

name: Neuropeculiar
summary: Italian association founded and directed by autistic people that campaigns for self-representation and self-determination under a neurodiversity and Disability Studies framework, and organises the annual AUTcamp gathering.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. No single stated headquarters; located at Rome, where its 2026 AUTcamp event is held.

name: Autisme- og Aspergerforeningen
summary: Danish national association describing itself as 'autisternes egen forening' (autistic people's own association), running local meeting places across the country, an annual Aukon conference, and disability-policy advocacy.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. No fixed single office; placed at a central Denmark coordinate. Automated curl checks returned a non-standard 454 status from this network; content was independently confirmed via fetch.

name: Autistic Mutual Aid Society Edinburgh (AMASE)
summary: Edinburgh-based Autistic People's Organisation whose full members are all autistic, running peer support, an online 'My Autism Story' event series, Autistic Pride and Weird Pride Day gatherings, and policy statements.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. Site states 'all full members are autistic.' Most events run online.

name: ARGH Scotland
summary: Scottish charitable incorporated organisation based in the Highlands whose committee and full voting members are all autistic, doing collective advocacy, lobbying and campaigning on autism services across Scotland.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. The listed EUCAP URL (arghscotland.co.uk) now redirects permanently to arghscotland.org, used here. Partners with the Scottish Government on autism strategy.

name: autSocial e.V.
summary: Hamburg-based German association run under the motto 'von Autist*innen für Autist*innen' (by autistic people for autistic people), operating self-help groups, online workshops on masking and workplace inclusion, and creative projects like autArt.
notes: Full member of EUCAP; funded in part through Hamburg's social affairs authority.

name: LAVA (Reading and Advisory Group of Adults with Autism)
name_local: Lees- en Adviesgroep Volwassenen met Autisme
summary: Ghent-based Flemish group of autistic adults that critically reviews autism research, advises on research priorities and media framing, and organises public lectures and reading salons on autism from a neurodiversity perspective.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. States 'we are adults with autism'; partners with Leuven Autism Research and the Flemish Autism Action Plan.

name: MTÜ Autistid
summary: Estonian association, established 2019 as the Estonian Autistic Women's Association, that spreads information about autism and neurodiversity, builds community, and advocates to improve conditions for autistic people in Estonia.
notes: Full member of EUCAP, formerly Eesti Autistlike Naiste Ühing (Estonian Autistic Women's Association), founded 8 March 2019. Site notes it is under renovation. The EUCAP-listed URL (eany.ee) redirects to autistid.ee, used here. Leadership not explicitly stated on-site as autistic-led, so marked unknown despite the association's name and history.

name: Organiserade Autister
summary: Swedish interest association of and for autistic people (formerly known as Organiserade Aspergare), running discussion groups and community activities and promoting neurodiversity and self-determination.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. Site describes itself as 'an interest association of and for autists.' Likely the current name of the organisation previously known as Organiserade Aspergare; no fixed city stated.

name: Suomen Autismikirjon Yhdistys (ASY)
summary: Helsinki-based Finnish association working for the wellbeing and equality of autistic people, running peer support groups, an autism-friendly certification programme, and summer and autumn community gatherings.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. Leadership composition not explicitly stated as autistic-led on the pages read, so marked unknown despite EUCAP full-member status.

name: A Centrum
summary: Slovak organisation running education, conferences and a self-advocacy programme ('Kľúče k sebaobhajobe') on autism, Asperger syndrome and neurodiversity, involving neurodivergent young people as volunteers and advocates.
notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Leads courses/podcasts through Viera Hincová; not explicitly stated whether the organisation itself is autistic-led.

name: suntAutist
summary: Romanian association publishing 'autism explained by autistics' articles by autistic contributors, opposing ABA and conversion-style therapies and offering resources for autistic children, women and men.
notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Tagline 'Autismul explicat de autiști' (autism explained by autistics); named autistic contributors write the site's articles. No fixed city stated.

name: Autminds
summary: Dutch congress for and by autistic people, run for eleven years out of Delft, bringing autistic adults together for talks, workshops and networking; its final edition is scheduled for October 2026.
notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Founding year inferred from the site's own '11 years' claim ahead of its announced final October 2026 congress; included despite the planned wind-down because it is still active as of verification.

name: National Autistic Taskforce (NAT)
summary: British autistic-run body, founded 2018, that campaigns for better services for autistic people with high support needs, publishing independent care-quality guides and running the EQUALS Project on decision-making support.
notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Describes itself as 'an innovative autistic-run body' focused on autistic people less able to self-advocate. No single headquarters city stated; placed at London as a national placeholder.

name: Jasna Strona Spektrum
summary: Polish autism information and support website for diagnosed and undiagnosed autistic children and adults, publishing articles on daily life, self-advocacy and diagnosis and running parent workshops.
notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Leadership not stated on the site; no fixed city given.

name: Autisme Ungdom
summary: Danish youth and disability organisation for autistic people aged 13-35, founded 2019 with a board composed entirely of young autistic people, running six regional chapters, a Discord community, and an annual summer camp.
notes: Associate member of EUCAP; found while cross-checking the EUCAP member list. Membership does not require a formal diagnosis.

name: AsIAm
summary: Ireland's national autism charity, founded in 2014 by autistic CEO Adam Harris, working on autism-friendly community certification, policy and self-advocacy, with a stated policy of at least half its board being autistic.
notes: Registered as a Disabled Persons' Organisation; runs the Autism Friendly Towns programme.

name: Scottish Autism
summary: Scotland's largest autism-specific service provider, founded in 1968 by a group of parents, running residential and day support, an advice line, family support and participatory research through its Centre for Practice, Policy and Research.
notes: Included as a large, well-known ally-led anchor organisation for Scotland, in contrast to the autistic-led ARGH Scotland and AMASE entries in this batch.

name: Autismus-Kultur
summary: German website written from an autistic perspective on how autistic people can live well in a non-autistic world, offering practical guidance, tips and community discussion rather than clinical advice.
notes: Site self-describes as written from an autistic perspective. Returns 403 to automated fetches (bot-blocking); reachable and returns 200 to a plain curl with a browser user agent. No stated headquarters city; placed at a geographic-centre-of-Germany coordinate as a placeholder.

name: Fundacja Autism Team
summary: Łódź-based Polish foundation, founded 2016, combining autistic people, families, experts and therapists to run youth and parent support clubs, crisis intervention, school inclusion programmes and creative 'Artegracja' projects.
notes: Site describes staff as 'osoby w spektrum autyzmu, ich rodziny, eksperci i terapeuci' (autistic people, their families, experts and therapists), hence marked mixed rather than nd-led.

name: ADHD Jersey
summary: Jersey (Channel Islands) not-for-profit combining lived ADHD experience with professional expertise, running adult and youth ADHD support programmes, awareness talks and a community hub in St Helier.
notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations. Site states it was 'built by people who truly understand ADHD because we've lived it,' combined with professional expertise.

name: Akrasia (Association for Adults with ADHD)
name_local: Spolek pro dospělé s diagnózou ADHD
summary: Czech association founded in 2022 by psychologists, some with personal ADHD experience, running a nationwide network of peer support groups, workshops and an online resource-navigation tool for adults with ADHD.
notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations. Also active in Brno and Pardubice.

name: Fundacja ADHD
summary: Polish foundation providing psychological consultations, ADHD and autism diagnostic assessments, crisis support and public education for neurodivergent people nationwide.
notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations. No single headquarters city stated.

name: NPF Åland
summary: Åland Islands association spreading knowledge about neuropsychiatric disabilities and advocating for the rights of people with them, running member support groups and a youth forum called Simuli.
notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations. Affiliated with Funktionsrätt Åland and ABF Åland.

name: Scottish ADHD Coalition
summary: Scottish charity, founded 2017 out of a 2016 Dundee meeting of local groups, coordinating voluntary organisations across Scotland that support adults and children with ADHD, including youth groups, parent training and referral information.
notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations, though the coalition itself dates to 2017. Registered Scottish charity SC047320.

name: Austrian Federal Association for Dyslexia (ÖBVL)
summary: Austrian dyslexia association providing certified training for dyslexia therapists, professional continuing education, therapist directories and public information on dyslexia.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Headquarters city not stated on the site; Vienna used as a national placeholder.

name: Ordblindeforeningen i Danmark
summary: Danish dyslexia association based in Taastrup, giving free professional guidance to individuals, schools and employers, running regional and youth chapters, and publishing a member magazine on dyslexia.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Patron since 2024 is Princess Marie of Denmark.

name: Association of Different Learners (FINDER)
summary: Helsinki-based Finnish association supporting people with dyslexia, dyscalculia and other learning difficulties in work and education, offering counselling, peer 'experience expert' activities and policy advocacy.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association.

name: French Federation of Dys Disorders (FFDys)
summary: French federation of regional associations for people with dyslexia, dyspraxia, dyscalculia and related developmental disorders, running an annual National Dys Day and professional training programme.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Its 20th National Dys Day fell in 2026. Site describes mobilising 'parents and professionals throughout France,' hence marked ally-led.

name: Federal Association for Dyslexia and Dyscalculia (BVL)
summary: German federal association, established around 1976, advocating for accommodations for people with dyslexia and dyscalculia in school, training and careers, with regional chapters and a therapist certification programme.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Founding year inferred from the site's own '50 years' anniversary claim.

name: British Dyslexia Association (BDA)
summary: English registered charity providing dyslexia and dyscalculia assessments, teacher training and accreditation, a helpline, and a Dyslexia Friendly Quality Mark for schools and workplaces.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Registered charity 289243.

name: Dyslexia Ireland
summary: Dublin-based Irish charity providing dyslexia and dyscalculia assessments, tutoring, training for parents and teachers, and policy advocacy, funded in part by the Department of Education.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Site returns 403 to some automated fetch tools (bot-blocking) but was read in full via a different fetch and confirmed live with a browser-header curl.

name: Italian Dyslexia Association (AID)
summary: Bologna-based Italian association, founded 1997, supporting people with specific learning disorders across their lifespan through teacher and family training, the LibroAID digital textbook platform, and school/workplace advocacy.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association.

name: Polish Dyslexia Society (PTD)
summary: Polish learned society on dyslexia running regional branches, an advisory clinic, and courses and training on specific learning difficulties, with an active branch in Gdańsk.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Site is mostly navigation/image-based; national headquarters not clearly stated, so located at its documented Gdańsk branch.

name: Dyslexiförbundet
summary: Swedish national federation for people with dyslexia and dyscalculia, based in Stockholm, offering educational and workplace guidance, a writing-support helpline, assistive-technology information and a member magazine.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Patron is Prince Carl Philip of Sweden.
